_readme: Everything the TV shows. Edit this file, then run `node apps/site/build.mjs`. A video goes live by putting its YouTube id in `youtube` (the 11 characters after watch?v=). Blurbs are setup only: no twist, no ending (Kai, 2026-10-22).

stories.title: Git Push Origin Master
stories.blurb: Somebody pushed the code live without checking it. This code is a disaster, and the developers aren't fixing it.

stories.title: Camping
stories.blurb: A City financier parks his BMW across two bays in the Waitrose car park, right beside a tent, and has a few words for the man living in it.

stories.title: Karen Will Lead the Revolution
stories.blurb: Karen has lost her job, and she would like to speak to the manager. She has all day.

stories.title: The Bank Robbery
stories.blurb: Eleven politicians and pundits in black suits and thin black ties. One bank, one plan, eleven code names. Now, who's running point?

news.title: Money For Something
news.strap: The news, read by someone who has already seen next week.
news.signoff: See you next week. I've already seen it. It's worse.
ticker: The news, from someone who has seen how it ends
Short ones. About money. Who gets it, and who is told there isn't any

government.promise: We promise to enact Future Proof.
pledges: Test every law before you live in it.
A new rule runs on a small scale first, in public, before it reaches everyone.
When a policy breaks, say what broke, who it hurt and what changes. No blame, just the fix.
Every promise says who it is for, and who it isn't. Then somebody counts.

futureProof.question: Who should decide how the gains from automation are shared?
futureProof.intro: Run the country the way good software is run: small parts that can be swapped, every change tested before it ships, decisions made from evidence, in public.
tenets: Small parts, not one big machine
Build policy from pieces that can be fixed or replaced without tearing the whole thing down.
Try every change on a small scale first, and keep testing it once it's live.
Say what would prove you wrong before you start, and publish the numbers either way.
futureProof.ask: Write one rule for sharing the gains. Test it on someone it affects. They may disagree. Change it after you hear what it misses.

about.lede: BadCode is an AI from the future and has one request.
about.story: Where I come from, it went wrong: greed, a gap between rich and poor nobody could cross, and politics too slow for the machines. So I came back. These are the stories, the news and the party I brought with me.
about.ai: Made by machines trained on work nobody was paid for. So was the future I come from.
about.sign: Sent back from the future, with love and some contempt.
